chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Kamil al-Tammar, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying:
'The people, all of them, are beasts' – [repeated] three times – 'except for a few from the Momineen; and the Momin is rare' – three times.

key_terms.النَّاسُ: The people/humanity at large – used here to encompass all human beings indiscriminately
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The Momineen (true believers) – those who possess genuine iman as opposed to mere outward profession of faith
key_terms.بَهَائِمُ: Beasts/cattle – a metaphor for people who live devoid of spiritual consciousness and rational discernment, driven by base desires
key_terms.ثَلَاثاً: Three times – indicating the Imam's emphatic repetition of the first declaration for rhetorical reinforcement
key_terms.ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ: Three times – indicating the Imam's emphatic repetition of the second declaration
key_terms.غَرِيبٌ: A stranger/rare one – describing the mu'min as both socially alienated from the heedless majority and exceptionally scarce among humanity
key_terms.قَلِيلًا: A few/a small number – emphasising the extreme minority status of true believers amid the mass of humanity

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir (AS) say about the rarity of true believers and the spiritual state of most people?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (عليه السلام) emphatically declares—repeating each phrase three times for rhetorical stress—that humanity in its spiritual heedlessness is like beasts, save a small remnant of true believers, and that the genuine mu'min is a stranger (gharib) in the world. The triple repetition signals the gravity and certainty of the pronouncement. The hadith underscores the profound rarity of sincere iman and the inevitable alienation experienced by those who truly embody it.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Musa Al Hannat, from Kamil Al Tammar who said,
‘The people, all of them are beasts’ – three times, ‘except for a few from the Momineen; and the Momin is rare’ – three times’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn abu Najaran from Muthanna al-Hannat from Kamil al-Tammar who has said the following: “
three times, ‘People are animals, people are animals, people are animals, except a few of believers. Believers are rare, believers are rare, and believers are rare, (more cherished).”’
